title: The_2028_Global_Intelligence_Crisis
summary:
The 2028 Global Intelligence Crisis is a report authored by James van Geelen and Alap Shah, published by Citrini Research in February 2026, on the impact of artificial intelligence on humanity's future. Written in the form of a scenario analysis from the perspective of June 2028 looking back, it was viewed millions of times online and helped trigger a sharp market selloff.

The report's central scenario imagines an AI-driven hollowing-out of white-collar work so severe that the circular flow of the economy stops functioning. GDP and profits rise, but households, cut out of the loop, stop spending. The authors dubbed this "Ghost GDP," output that appears in national accounts but does not circulate through the people who used to earn it. In the scenario, the S&P 500 peaks near 8,000 in 2026 before underlying consumer demand evaporates, triggering a deflationary depression. By mid-2027, the US economy tips into a recession and by 2028, unemployment exceeds 10 percent.

On Monday, February 23, 2026, the speculative memo helped trigger a sharp risk-off move that wiped billions off the value of US-listed firms. Michael Burry amplified it on X with the comment "And you think I'm bearish." IBM fell about 13% on the day. The Wall Street Journal pointed to the viral report as a key accelerant of investor anxiety, and discussion racked up roughly 16 million views on X.

Critics noted that the Citrini scenario only modeled labor substitution, not capability creation. The scenario requires uneven diffusion, monopolization, and policy failure to all fail simultaneously within roughly two years, which the authors acknowledged as a specific left-tail outcome in their preface.
